Definition: from G3173; to make (or declare) great, i.e. increase or (figuratively) extol:--enlarge, magnify, shew great.
BiblicalUsage: To magnify is to make great, and the Bible uses it for God and for men: Mary says my soul doth magnify the Lord, and Elizabeth's neighbours magnify God for the mercy shown to her. The Pharisees enlarge their phylacteries to be seen, and Paul says Christ shall be magnified in his body, whether by life or by death.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe magnifying is the choice every life makes: Mary magnified the Lord, the Pharisees magnified themselves, and Paul magnified Christ in his body. What we make great is what we worship, and the soul that magnifies God finds itself made great by Him.
RelatedPeople: Mary, Mother of Jesus; Elizabeth; Jesus; Paul
RelatedEvents: The Birth of John the Baptist
